newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - Apr 25.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - Apr 25.

text.p: News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Brand-name Products, and Media

FRANKFURT - Western Germany is still buying hardly any food from Eastern Germany, the BVS German privatisation agency says. Chairman of the BVS advisory board Klaus von Dohnanyi says that, seven years after German unification, east German firms represent only one percent of the retail food sales in the western part of the country. (Reuter)

HAMBURG - Advertising agency Wilkens Hamburg GmbH says it has won the account of Munich-based lingerie manufacturer Triumph International. Wilkens will begin work on the estimated 15 million mark ($8.7 million) account on May 1. (Reuter)
HAMBURG - Pay-television service Premiere hopes to escape spiralling film prices by investing more in co-productions with German and foreign stations. (Die Welt)

MUNICH - Media-Analyse (MA), Germany's largest poll on magazine and newspaper readership, says the Munich-based Sueddeutsche Zeitung boosted its number of readers this year to 1.23 million, up 20,000 from 1996. (Sueddeutsche Zeitung)

BERLIN - Mineral water prices could soon rise by up to 50 pfennigs per case, the Association of German Mineral Springs (VDM) says. Sales plummeted by 100 million marks last year to 4.7 billion marks, VDM says, due in large part to a cool, rainy summer. (Reuter)

DUESSELDORF - Bathroom fittings manufacturer Friedrich Grohe AG says it is aiming to raise its annual sales by about 50 percent to 1.8 billion marks by the turn of the century through acquisitions in Europe in America. The company says it is prepared to spend about 300 marks on acquisitions. (Reuter)

HERZOGENAURACH - Puma AG says its sales and profits rose in the first quarter and dismissed shareholder worries that the German sportswear group was striving too hard for record profits. Puma says pre-tax profit for the quarter rose to 30.6 million marks from 27.7 million marks in the 1996 first quarter while net sales rose 3.6 percent to 153.6 million marks from 148.3 million marks in the year-ago period. (Reuter)
